chapter_title: The Building Blocks of Schools, Students, and Learning
learning_objective: The learner will examine how the pitch of a single whole-class lesson determines how many students in a mixed-readiness class are in reach, too far behind, or already ahead, and identify the pitch that reaches the most students.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** one-lesson-many-readiness-levels
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** examine
**Learning Objective:** The learner will examine how the pitch of a single whole-class lesson determines how many students in a mixed-readiness class are in reach, too far behind, or already ahead, and identify the pitch that reaches the most students. **Prerequisites:** learning gap, direct instruction, classroom, readiness expressed as a grade level, the "in reach" rule (all defined in the section "The Learning Gap" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner answers three questions with committed answers: (Q1) the pitch that puts the most students in reach — correct answer 7; (Q2) the number of students in reach at that best pitch — correct answer 13; (Q3) the number of students at pitch 7 for whom the lesson is too hard — correct answer 7. Mastery is 3 of 3. Moving the pitch freely is exploration. **Misconceptions:** (1) Teaching "to the middle" reaches most of the class. (2) A skilled enough teacher can find one pitch that works for everyone. (3) Students ahead of the lesson are learning something; in this model they are waiting. **Instructional Rationale:** Analyzing requires the learner to see how one variable (pitch) splits a fixed group into parts. Predicting before exploring, then testing every pitch, lets the learner discover for themselves that the best single pitch still misses more than half the class. **Content:** Class of 28 students, each shown as an individual marker grouped by readiness: | Readiness (grade level) | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Students | 1 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 7 | 5 | 2 | 1 | Three student states, with the label shown in the legend: - In reach: the lesson is at the student's readiness level or one level above. - Too hard: the lesson is more than one level above the student's readiness. - Already known: the lesson is below the student's readiness. In-reach counts for every pitch, used to check the sim: | Pitch | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | In reach | 1 | 3 | 6 | 10 | 13 | 12 | 7 | 3 | **Provenance:** The class distribution is illustrative, written for this chapter; the sim must label it "Illustrative class." The in-reach rule is defined in the chapter section "The Learning Gap." **Rules:** Lesson pitch p: min 3, max 10, step 1, default 7, unit grade level. For a student with readiness r: in reach when 0 <= p − r <= 1; too hard when p − r > 1; already known when p − r < 0. Counts are recomputed whenever p changes. The best pitch is the one with the highest in-reach count; in this class it is unique (p = 7). **Learner Activity:** 1. Before the pitch can be changed, the learner answers Q1 and Q2 as predictions. 2. The learner moves the pitch from 3 to 10. Each student marker changes state and the three counts update at once. 3. The learner should notice that the in-reach count rises to 13 at pitch 7 and falls on either side, and that at every pitch at least 15 students are too hard or already known. 4. The learner sets the pitch to 7 and answers Q3. 5. The learner submits all three answers for checking. **Feedback:** Three questions, fixed order, two attempts each. Q1 correct: "Yes — pitch 7 puts 13 students in reach, the most of any pitch." Q1 incorrect: "Try each pitch and watch the in-reach count; it peaks at one value." Q2 correct: "Right — 13 of 28, fewer than half the class." Q2 incorrect: "Count the students at readiness 6 and 7 when the pitch is 7." Q3 correct: "Correct — the 7 students at readiness 3, 4 and 5 are more than one level behind." Q3 incorrect: "Count students whose readiness is more than one level below the pitch." After the second wrong attempt, the answer and its explanation are shown. A score "n of 3" is shown after submission. **Starting State:** The pitch is at 7 but locked, all 28 markers are shown by readiness without state colors, and the prompt reads "Where should one lesson be pitched to reach the most students — and how many will it reach?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter uses a class of 28 with the distribution above, pitches the lesson at grade 7, and states that 13 students are in reach, 7 find it too hard, and 8 already know it. The chapter states that no single pitch reaches more than 13 of the 28 students.
